claims.claim: Augustine of Hippo was a presbyter when he delivered this discourse.
Augustine was bishop of Hippo from 396 to 430.
The work was originally a discourse delivered before a council of the whole North African Episcopate assembled at Hippo-Regius.
The Council of Hippo-Regius took place in 393 A.D.
Augustine was requested to deliver the discourse in public by the bishops assembled at the council.
The discourse was subsequently issued as a book at the desire of friends.

The council was historically important for its protest against the position allowed to Patriarchs elsewhere in the Church and against any more authoritative title than simply Bishop of the first Church.
The work provides a fuller treatment of the brief Creed memorized by new Christians to protect it against heretics.
The work addresses controversies including those who posit uncreated matter, those who identify the Son with the Father or call him a creature, and those who deny Christ had a human mother.
